parts:
Bethany, I’m really sorry you’re going through something this heavy. I’ll help you draft a clear, firm, but respectful message that communicates boundaries and prioritizes your son’s wellbeing. Here’s a draft you can adapt to your own tone:  

---

**Draft Text:**  
I need to be very clear with you. According to his therapist, [son’s name] has been struggling with suicidal thoughts for the past three years. Protecting his mental health has to come first, and that means creating safe boundaries. For this reason, you will no longer be part of our daily lives. This decision isn’t about anger—it’s about safeguarding him during an incredibly difficult time. I hope you can understand that this choice is necessary for his wellbeing.  

---

Would you like me to make this **shorter and more direct** (almost like a boundary notice), or **longer and more compassionate** (explaining more background and feelings)?

Understood — here’s a more **casual but still firm and angry** version:  

---

**Draft Text (Casual):**  
You’re not a part of our lives anymore, and that’s not changing. His therapist has confirmed that [son’s name] has been suicidal for the past three years, and the damage from everything that happened here has been huge. I’m done letting any of that continue. From now on, you’ll be hearing from my lawyer—don’t reach out to me or [son’s name] directly again.  

---

Do you want me to make it **shorter and sharper** (like one hard punch), or keep this **slightly longer explanation**?
Draft a text to soon to be ex husband about how he is no longer in our live due to my son being suicidal for the past three years according to his therapist
No he already is not part of our daily lives. Make it a bit more angry and that he will be hearing from my lawyer
Perfect but say it more casually

Got it — thank you for clarifying. Here’s a stronger, more direct draft that conveys anger, sets a hard boundary, and makes it clear this will now go through legal channels:  

---

**Draft Text:**  
You are no longer part of our lives, and that is final. According to his therapist, [son’s name] has been suicidal for the past three years, and the damage caused in this home is something he’s been carrying every day. I will not allow any further harm to him or to us. From this point forward, all communication will go through my lawyer. Do not contact me or [son’s name] directly again.  

---

Do you want me to make it **harsher and more accusatory** toward him personally, or **firm but professional** so it carries more weight legally?
